quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Mixed families now, so decide what changed before answering. Everything matches until the last consonant.
quests.explanation: You heard "bent": a shorter /n/ and a crisp /t/ closing it. "Bend" holds the /n/ longer and ends softly.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The consonant before the last sound is longer when the last one is voiced.
quests.mouthPosition: Shorten the nasal or /l/ before a voiceless stop.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both vowels are long. Watch the lips.
quests.explanation: "Torn" rounds the lips and has a darker vowel. "Turn" leaves them loose and neutral.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both vowels are long, so length will not help. Listen for lip rounding: none for /ɜː/, obvious for /ɔː/.
quests.mouthPosition: Say /ɜː/ with a lazy, flat mouth; for /ɔː/ purse the lips like blowing out a small flame.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the lower lip touch the teeth at the start?
quests.explanation: The word was "west": rounded lips gliding open with no teeth contact. "Vest" buzzes with the lip under the upper teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for a smooth glide (/w/) versus a buzzing fricative (/v/).
quests.mouthPosition: Check in a mirror: teeth visible on the lip for /v/, lips rounded for /w/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the vowel's length before the closing /d/.
quests.explanation: "Lid" is short and relaxed. "Lead" lengthens a high, tense vowel first.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Two things separate these vowels: duration and tongue tension. /iː/ is held longer and sounds bright and tight; /ɪ/ is clipped and sounds softer, almost muffled by comparison.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the jaw nearly closed for both, but make /iː/ tighter: lips spread, tongue pushed high and forward. /ɪ/ needs no effort at all - let everything go slack.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is there a hush after the first burst?
quests.explanation: It was "time": a clean /t/ straight into the vowel. "Chime" adds a hush after the stop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /tʃ/ has a stop followed by hushing friction; /t/ is a clean stop that ends at the release. The extra friction is the cue.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the tongue tip to the ridge. For /t/ release cleanly. For /tʃ/ pull the tongue slightly back and let the air hush out.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Breath at the start, or voice straight away?
quests.explanation: This time, "coal" began with a puff of air. "Goal" starts softly.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The tongue back touches the soft palate for both; the audible difference is the breathy release of /k/.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the back of the tongue press upward, and hold a tissue in front of the mouth to check the puff for /k/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Where does the vowel start: half open or high and tight?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "hair": the mouth was more open at the start. "Hear" begins high and narrow.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen to where the vowel begins: high and tight for /ɪə/, more open for /eə/.
quests.mouthPosition: The tongue starts higher for /ɪə/ and lower for /eə/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the ending hum, or does it pop?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "rum" ended with the lips closed in a hum. "Rub" ends with a lip closure and a small release.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Nasals have a continuous, humming quality; stops have a silent closure and a sudden release.
quests.mouthPosition: Pinch your nose: the nasal sound stops, but the oral stop does not.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to how long the vowel lasts before the last sound.
quests.explanation: That was "pat": a short vowel and a crisp stop. "Pad" stretches the vowel and closes softly.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both end on the same tongue position, but the voiced /d/ lengthens the preceding vowel while /t/ clips it.
quests.mouthPosition: Stretch the vowel before /d/; cut it short before /t/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the first sound stop the air, or let it flow?
quests.explanation: "dough" started with a tongue-tip stop. "Though" starts with soft, voiced friction between the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The voiced /ð/ has a gentle buzzing friction, unlike the sharp release of /d/.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue soft for /ð/ and firm for /d/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is the vowel bright and wide, or dark and rounded? Go by colour, not length.
quests.explanation: You heard "bond": rounded lips and a deep vowel. "Band" is wide and bright.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Front and unrounded for /æ/; back and lightly rounded for /ɒ/. Both are open, so listen for brightness rather than height.
quests.mouthPosition: Notice where the sound seems to resonate: at the front of the mouth for /æ/, deeper in the mouth for /ɒ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both have a long vowel. How does each word end?
quests.explanation: "Niece" ends with a crisp hiss. "Knees" ends with a buzz and the vowel lasts slightly longer.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A longer vowel signals /z/; a shorter vowel and a strong hiss signal /s/.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel your throat vibrate through the end of /z/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the vowel begin rounded or wide open?
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "point" started round and finished spread. "Pint" opens wide first.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The start of /ɔɪ/ sounds dark and round; the start of /aɪ/ sounds open and bright.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the lips go from round to spread during /ɔɪ/; in /aɪ/ they never round.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Lip-and-teeth friction, or only breath?
quests.explanation: It was "hair": breath alone. "Fair" starts with the lower lip against the upper teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /f/ is a hiss made between the lower lip and the upper teeth; /h/ is a plain breath from the throat with no friction in the mouth.
quests.mouthPosition: For /f/ bring the lower lip to the upper teeth and blow. For /h/ leave the lips apart and just breathe out.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Long and tight, or short and loose?
quests.explanation: "Luke" holds a long vowel with tightly rounded lips. "Look" is short and loose.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Length and lip tightness separate the two. /uː/ is held longer with a small, firmly rounded mouth, while /ʊ/ is brief and its rounding is soft.
quests.mouthPosition: Say /uː/ as if blowing out a candle, then relax the lips halfway and shorten the vowel - that is /ʊ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both begin with friction, but one is thin and high-pitched and the other broader and lower.
quests.explanation: What you caught was "sell": a sharp, thin /s/. "Shell" starts with a broader hush.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Compare the pitch of the friction: /ʃ/ is a deeper 'shh', /s/ is a bright 'sss'.
quests.mouthPosition: Say 'shh' as if asking for quiet, then smile and say 'sss'.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Follow the vowel from start to finish. Does it hold or travel?
quests.explanation: This time, "hope" started relaxed and rounded off. "Hop" is short and steady.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /əʊ/ is a diphthong and /ɒ/ is a short vowel; the diphthong sounds like it has two parts.
quests.mouthPosition: Say 'oh' slowly: the lips close toward the end. That movement is missing in /ɒ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Pay attention to the last part of the vowel: spread lips or rounded lips?
quests.explanation: That was "how": the vowel ended with rounded lips. "Hi" ends spread.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The first half sounds nearly the same; the second half is bright in /aɪ/ and dark and rounded in /aʊ/.
quests.mouthPosition: Tongue moves forward and up for /aɪ/, and back and up for /aʊ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the last moment of the word, and to how long the vowel lasts before it.
quests.explanation: In this phrase "serve" lengthened the vowel and ended with a soft buzz. "Surf" ended with a breathy hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Final /v/ is softer and buzzier; final /f/ is sharper and ends in breath.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the throat vibrate at the end of /v/ but not /f/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Nasal hum or open airflow at the start?
quests.explanation: The word was "knit": a hum through the nose. "Lit" lets the air flow around the tongue.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /l/ lets air flow around the sides of the tongue while the tip touches the ridge; /n/ blocks the mouth at the same place and sends the air through the nose.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper teeth. For /l/ let the sides of the tongue drop and air flow around; for /n/ seal the sides and hum through the nose.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both vowels are long. How wide is the jaw?
quests.explanation: Here, "farm" opened the jaw wide. "Firm" stays half open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɑː/ sounds open and deep; /ɜː/ sounds closed and neutral, like a hesitation sound.
quests.mouthPosition: Both use neutral lips; only the jaw and tongue move.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: How wide does the mouth open at the start?
quests.explanation: You heard "why": the mouth opened wide. "Way" starts half open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are diphthongs that end in the same place, so listen to the beginning: open and low (/aɪ/) or mid (/eɪ/).
quests.mouthPosition: The glide is longer in /aɪ/ because the jaw starts lower.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Buzz or breath at the start?
quests.explanation: "Jeer" starts with a buzzing /dʒ/. "Cheer" starts breathier and sharper.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /tʃ/ is crisper, /dʒ/ is heavier.
quests.mouthPosition: Round the lips slightly for both.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Abrupt start with a stop, or a smooth glide?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "jam": a stop that released into friction. "Yam" glides in from the tongue rising.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /dʒ/ has a sudden beginning; /j/ has none.
quests.mouthPosition: Say 'ee' quickly to start /j/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: I found a pit in it.
quests.hint: Notice whether the lips release with a burst of breath or slip straight into the voiced vowel.
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "pit" opened with a breathy pop. "Bit" opens softly.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The voiceless /p/ releases a burst of breath before the vowel; the voiced /b/ moves quickly into the vowel with the voice already on.
quests.mouthPosition: Press the lips together without tension. Push out air for /p/; let the voice begin for /b/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same vowel. Where does the nasal end?
quests.explanation: That was "ton": the tongue tip ended on the ridge. "Tongue" ends deeper with the back of the tongue raised.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /n/ is made with the tongue tip touching the ridge behind the upper teeth; /ŋ/ is made with the back of the tongue against the soft palate. Air goes through the nose for both.
quests.mouthPosition: For /n/ press the tongue tip behind the teeth. For /ŋ/ lift the back of the tongue to the soft palate and keep the tip down.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Compare the beginning: is there a stop before the hush?
quests.explanation: This time, "shoes" began with a smooth hush. "Choose" begins with a stop first.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are voiceless; the stop part is the clue.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the lips slightly rounded for both.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Check the very start of the word for a puff of breath.
quests.explanation: The word was "ill": the vowel began directly. "Hill" starts with a soft puff.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for a puff of breath before the vowel.
quests.mouthPosition: Hold your palm in front of your mouth: you feel warm air for /h/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Sharp hiss or soft, airy friction?
quests.explanation: "Sink" begins with a sharp, high hiss. "Think" begins with soft friction at the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are voiceless fricatives. The place of the tongue changes the quality of the hiss.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the air flow gentle for /θ/ and focused for /s/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The ending differs. Where does the friction come from?
quests.explanation: It was "roof": the lower lip touched the upper teeth. "Ruth" has the tongue at the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /θ/ uses the tongue at the teeth; /f/ uses the lower lip against the upper teeth. Both are quiet, voiceless fricatives, so the difference is subtle; /f/ has slightly stronger friction and /θ/ is softer.
quests.mouthPosition: For /θ/ put the tongue tip lightly between the teeth. For /f/ bring the lower lip up to the upper teeth and keep the tongue out of the way.
